primary_metric_justification: Macro-averaged F1 is the primary classification metric, declared before any model was fitted. The six CPCB buckets are imbalanced by a factor of 6.6 between the most and least frequent class, and the rarest classes are Good and Severe. Severe is the class on which the entire public-health purpose of the system rests: failing to warn on a Severe day is the costliest error the system can make, and it is also the error that overall accuracy is least sensitive to. Macro-F1 gives every class equal weight regardless of frequency, so a model cannot score well by ignoring the rare and dangerous classes. Accuracy, weighted F1, per-class F1, balanced accuracy, Cohen's kappa and one-versus-rest ROC-AUC are all reported alongside it, together with an ordinal error that measures how many severity bands a wrong prediction lands away from the truth.
validation: TimeSeriesSplit with 4 expanding-window folds, scored by macro-F1. SMOTE is applied inside the imbalanced-learn pipeline so that resampling occurs within each training fold only.

leakage_demonstration.conclusion: Predicting the same day's bucket with same-day AQI present yields a macro-F1 of 1.0000. A score at or near 1.0 is not a result; it is the signature of a model reading its own label, because the CPCB bucket is a deterministic step function of the AQI. The more instructive finding is what happens after the obvious culprits are removed: dropping AQI, the CPCB sub-indices and every HAI column still leaves macro-F1 at 0.9666. The leak is therefore not confined to a single column that a diligent analyst could blacklist. The AQI is by definition the maximum sub-index, and each sub-index is a fixed piecewise-linear function of a pollutant concentration, so the *concentrations themselves* determine the label exactly. Same-day bucket prediction is arithmetic dressed as machine learning, and no choice of feature filter rescues it. That is the reason this project does not attempt it. Forecasting the next day changes the problem substantively: tomorrow's bucket is genuinely unknown today, today's AQI becomes legitimate information rather than a restatement of the answer, and the achieved macro-F1 of 0.7077 measures real predictive skill. The gap between 0.9666 and 0.7077 is the difference between recomputing a known quantity and forecasting an unknown one.
